title: Rainfall — daily CHIRPS over South America

options.content:
# Daily rainfall over South America

Sixty days of satellite precipitation (**CHIRPS**, 0.05°), one per bar of the timeline. Drag it and the map shows that day's rain; the curves on the right tell you where to look, because a peak in **intensity** or in **area with rain** is a day worth opening.

None of this was downloaded whole: CHIRPS publishes one COG per day, and DuckDB read over HTTP only the nine tiles that cover the continent, clipped them, and left them ready for the map.

**Two things worth knowing about what you are seeing.** The sheet is quantised — 0 to 30 mm over an integer — because kepler will not draw a floating-point raster: **above 30 mm in a day the shade stops distinguishing**, although the figures on the right, computed on the original data, do reach the 300 mm that fall on some days. And **everything** is painted, including where it did not rain, in the lightest shade: a field drawn only where it rains reads as noise rather than as weather. The ocean falls into that same light shade even though CHIRPS does not measure at sea — masking it would need a clip against the coastline.

panels.description: One COG per day. The timeline picks which one is drawn, and the handover between scenes overlaps, so dragging does not flicker.

targets.rawSql:
-- Una fila por día: la fecha, el COG de ese día y las tres cifras que lo
-- resumen. El mismo resultado alimenta el timeline, el mapa y las curvas, así
-- que arrastrar la barra no pide nada al servidor.
SELECT
  dia::TIMESTAMPTZ                    AS time,
  raster_url,
  round(intensidad_mm, 1)             AS intensidad_mm,
  round(fraccion_con_lluvia * 100, 1) AS area_con_lluvia_pct,
  round(max_mm, 0)                    AS max_mm
FROM read_parquet('/derived/chirps-index.parquet')
ORDER BY time

panels.title: The day's rain · drag the time bar

panels.description: Computed on the original floating-point rasters, before quantising: the intensity is the mean of the cells that recorded rain, not of the whole region.
